content.text:
I submitted index 19 (In 0.35 / Sb 0.65) as the best composition. Its EQE of 0.081% was the highest of the three I measured, but every value was low and the three were close together.

| Index | In / Sb | EQE (%) | What XRD showed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | 0.78 / 0.22 | 0.066 | Two phases: In₂O₃ plus a rutile-type phase |
| 19 | 0.35 / 0.65 | **0.081** | Only the rutile-type phase |
| 24 | 0.20 / 0.80 | 0.058 | Not scanned |

- **Why these three:** I measured index 6 first because the stability model puts In₁₁Sb₃O₂₄ at that composition exactly on the stability limit. Index 19 is near In₃Sb₅O₁₂, which the model puts just above it (0.018 eV/atom).
- **Band gaps:** the predicted gaps for all these phases are 1.9–2.8 eV, below the 3.2 eV illumination, so none should fail for lack of absorption.
- **Last measurement:** I spent it on index 24 because EQE had risen toward the Sb-rich side. It came out lower, so the peak seems to be somewhere around the middle of the line.
- **Phase matching:** at index 19 the peaks fit a rutile structure, but the match to the listed In–Sb phases was weak (similarity 0.18 or less), so the phase there isn't pinned down.

**Main gap:** the 50/50 region (indices 14–17) was never measured, and neither was the In-rich end. The curve-fitting model's last suggestion was index 22, and its second choice, index 16, falls in that 50/50 region. A better composition there is possible. The full merit budget is used; 3 of the 5 XRD scans are left.
